title: Teaching
text:
As someone believing in the open source philosophy, I keep my course contents open to public. If they turn out to help you, it would be great if you could also consider sharing what you know with people! 
I started the project <bereyhi-courses> in 2025 to unify all my courses for better access and maintenance. The first item is the course Deep Generative Models which started in May 2025 for the first time at UofT. My other courses were gradually migrated to this project.

title: Current Research
text:
Bayes Optimal Learning Threshold (BOLT) introduces a novel approach to design loss function: it derives a parameterized upper bound on the Bayes error rate and using its minimization to guide model training toward Bayes-optimal performance. Originally developed for classification, the BOLT framework has been extended to generative adversarial networks (BOLT-GAN). BOLT shows improved training stability and generative performance. Its underlying principle provides a general foundation for designing learning objectives across different learning problems. The original BOLT work received the Best Student Paper Award at IEEE ICASSP 2025.

BOLT: Universal Classifier Training via a Bayes-Error Upper Bound, Mohammadreza Tavasoli Naeini, Ali Bereyhi, Morteza Noshad, Ben Liang, Alfred O. Hero III | 2026 | Link
Revisiting GAN with Bayes-Optimal Discrimination, Mohammadreza Tavasoli Naeini, Ali Bereyhi, Morteza Noshad, Ben Liang, Alfred O. Hero III | 2026 | Link




Communication overhead is a major bottleneck in distributed learning, particularly over wireless networks. Our research addresses this challenge through the development of communication-efficient techniques, including gradient sparsification, device scheduling, and over-the-air aggregation. Beyond reducing communication costs, we investigate the fundamental role of aggregation errors in distributed learning. In particular, our Global Unknown Estimation framework interprets distributed aggregation as a statistical estimation problem, highlighting that conventional computation-error metrics do not necessarily reflect the impact of aggregation on learning performance. Instead, the bias and variance of aggregation errors provide a more meaningful characterization, motivating new approaches to the design and optimization of distributed learning systems.

Regularized Top-k: A Bayesian Framework for Gradient Sparsification, Ali Bereyhi, Ben Liang, Gary Boudreau, Ali Afana
IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing | 2025 | Link




Many problems in signal processing share mathematical structures with those encountered in machine learning, creating opportunities to leverage learning-inspired techniques for efficient system design and optimization. Our research explores these connections to address various challenges in wireless communications and sensing, including array design, precoding, resource allocation, and object detection. UUtilizing machine learning techniques along with model-based signal processing, we develop computationally-efficient approaches to address key design problems in these domains.

Recent advances in machine learning have opened new opportunities for addressing complex problems in prediction, optimization, and decision-making. Our research investigates how modern learning paradigms, including foundation models, generative modeling, and reinforcement learning, can be leveraged to address such challenges. We are particularly interested in understanding the capabilities and limitations of these approaches and developing methods that improve their effectiveness, reliability, and adaptability in real-world applications, with a particular emphasis on finance and automation.

text:
Recent advances in machine learning have opened new opportunities for addressing complex problems in prediction, optimization, and decision-making. Our research investigates how modern learning paradigms, including foundation models, generative modeling, and reinforcement learning, can be leveraged to address such challenges. We are particularly interested in understanding the capabilities and limitations of these approaches and developing methods that improve their effectiveness, reliability, and adaptability in real-world applications, with a particular emphasis on finance and automation.

I am Assistant Professor (TS) in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Toronto. I am also Faculty Affiliate at Schwartz Reisman Institute (SRI). My main area of focus is Machine Learning (ML) and Information Theory. My teachings cover a wide scope of topics in theory and applications of machine learning learning, ranging from Deep Learning and Statistical Methods to Reinforcement Learning and Generative Models. My research focuses on fundamental limits of ML models and their applications to Statistical Signal Processing.
I received my PhD (in German Doktor der Ingenieurwissenschaft) with distinction from Friedrich Alexander Universität (FAU) in Germany, supervised by Prof. Dr.-Ing. Ralf R. Müller and Prof. Dr. Hermann Schulz-Baldes. My doctoral dissertation, entitled Statistical Mechanics of Regularized Least Squares, investigates the connections between Theoretical Physics and the Theory of Learning. You can also find me on the Mathematics Genealogy Project!



Perspective graduate students are welcome to contact me by email. You can take a look at the current research in my team.


Those who are interested in graduate research projects either in the form of Research Internship or MEng Research Module, e.g., ECE2500, may reach out through email.

There are currently open projects on Quantum Machine Learning and AI Safety
New: I am looking for motivated Master’s students to join a research on Safety Risks Associated with Malicious Coordination among AI Agents. The position is full-time, starting as soon as possible and ending on March 2027. The project can be undertaken as part of the MEng Research Module. If interested, please send me a brief introduction and your CV by email.




Unfortunately, I am not able to respond to all application emails. If you don’t hear back from me in a course of one week or so, it is safe to consider the case closed. In that case, please accept my sincere apology for not being responsive to your email. I wish you all success with your application and thank you for taking time to write to me.
